findings.claim: In zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, refreshOAuthTokens is passed credentialId (credential.id) as its third argument, which is userId. The sync endpoint therefore receives the wrong calcomUserId.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:53,62,85-94, credential.id is assigned to credentialId and passed as the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens, whereas packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3,11 expects userId and sends it as calcomUserId to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT.

findings.claim: The webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison.

verifier.reason: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-26, the incoming webhook secret header is compared directly against process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET using !== rather than a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingSafeEqual.

findings.claim: parseRefreshTokenResponse sets a missing refresh_token to the literal string 'refresh_token'. Callers such as office365calendar and Zoom then persist it over the real stored refresh token.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27, any missing/falsy refresh_token is overwritten with the literal string "refresh_token". Callers then overwrite and persist the stored refresh_token via prisma.credential.update in packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-272 (where refresh_token is optional at line 56) and packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:104,120-124.

findings.claim: googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts stores the entire parseRefreshTokenResponse safeParse wrapper ({success, data, ...}) as Credential.key instead of its .data. The next googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) then throws.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:16-29, parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod safeParse result object ({ success: true, data }) rather than .data, and packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101 saves that wrapper directly into Credential.key. On subsequent loads, packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 calls googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key), which throws because packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/googleCredentialSchema.ts:3-9 requires top-level scope, token_type, expiry_date, access_token, and refresh_token fields.

findings.claim: The credential's invalid flag is never reset when the credential is updated.

verifier.reason: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:72-80, prisma.credential.update only updates `key: keys` and never resets `invalid: false` (likewise OAuth refresh updates such as packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:98-101 only update `key`). Because invalid credentials are skipped for availability checks in packages/core/getCalendarsEvents.ts:14-17 and flagged in the UI, a previously invalidated credential remains permanently marked invalid even after fresh keys are synced.

findings.claim: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on parse failure and never returns success: false. The !success branches in Salesforce getClient and Zoom are therefore dead code.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23, parseRefreshTokenResponse throws an Error whenever !refreshTokenResponse.success, so it can never return success: false. Consequently, the !accessTokenParsed.success branch in packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:90-94 and the !parsedToken.success branch in packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:104-110 are unreachable dead code.
